image.subject: Niall Ferguson, a British historian in his fifties, short greying hair, dark sport jacket over an open-collar shirt, seated at a wooden desk with books and a stack of old ledgers beside him

storyboard.claim: Information and money move across borders, so power today is shaped by that movement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at his desk with books and ledgers, the subject of the next idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Rothschild courier thread and turns it toward today.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the chapter as a question about modern power.

image.subject: a gilded quill pen resting on a printed 1815 map of Europe in a candle-lit palace study, a line of fresh ink drawn across the map

storyboard.claim: Kings draw borders on maps with their pens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quill drawing a border across a printed map of Europe.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the contrast between kings and networks.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kings hold the pen that draws borders.

image.subject: a leather purse spilling gold coins across an open ledger in a Frankfurt counting house with tall shelves behind it, dim winter light from a window

storyboard.claim: Financial networks control whether borders survive, not the kings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A purse of gold coins on a ledger in a counting house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the pen image: the pen draws, the purse decides.
storyboard.addedInformation: Money decides whether the borders hold.

storyboard.claim: States must pay for armies, peace and infrastructure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three cost items listed in plain type.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the kings had to pay for.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three big state costs.

storyboard.claim: Taxes arrive once a year but armies are paid every day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A large two-part number contrast in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the gap that forces states to borrow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The timing mismatch is the core problem.

image.subject: a row of sovereign bond certificates stacked on a banker's desk, each printed with a royal crest, in a Frankfurt counting house

storyboard.claim: The Rothschild network came to dominate the sovereign bond market.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stacked royal bond certificates on a banker's desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cash gap leads to borrowing through bonds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the bond market the network controlled.

image.subject: a Victorian London newspaper kiosk at dusk, broadsheets stacked under a gas lamp, a few pedestrians in dark wool coats passing by

storyboard.claim: Jump forward to 1894 London.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Victorian newspaper kiosk under a gas lamp at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the story from the bond market to the press of the 1890s.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the date and city for the cartoon that follows.

image.subject: a stack of 1890s London broadsheet newspapers folded open to a page of printed political cartoons, black ink on yellowed paper

storyboard.claim: A famous 1894 anti-Rothschild political cartoon circulated in the press.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Yellowed broadsheet pages with printed cartoon panels.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Points to the cartoon the host is about to describe.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cartoon was printed press material.

image.subject: a heavy brass-bound chest of gold coins, its lid open, in a dim 19th-century counting house with a shuttered window

storyboard.claim: The cartoon depicts a menacing force feeding on gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open chest of gold coins in dim light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the cartoon's gold imagery in place of the creature itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the gold that the cartoon's creature was feeding on.

image.subject: an antique terrestrial globe on a wooden stand in a London library, lit by a single lamp, its painted continents worn at the edges

storyboard.claim: The network seemed to reach every continent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worn antique globe lit by one lamp.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the cartoon's reach to a real object.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the global reach visible.

left.label: THE TOWER
left.subject: a stone royal palace at dusk with lit windows and guards standing at a closed iron gate

right.label: THE SQUARE
right.subject: a crowded 19th-century European town square at dusk, revolutionary banners hanging above cobblestones

storyboard.claim: A decentralized network looked terrifying to vertical towers of power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two pictures side by side: a closed royal palace gate and a crowded square.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the tower-square contrast the cartoon embodies.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the viewer both sides of the power contrast.

storyboard.claim: The Rothschilds had no army, king or country yet touched everything.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A rhetorical question in text.
storyboard.onScreenText: NO ARMY / NO KING / NO COUNTRY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the towers feared the network.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists what the Rothschilds lacked.

storyboard.claim: Refusing to buy a nation's debt could ruin its economy, making the network subversive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bold closing line in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question just asked.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the lever the network held over states.

image.subject: an ordinary person of mid-thirties in plain clothes, seen from behind, standing in a crowded town square at dusk and looking up at a tall stone tower

storyboard.claim: The square appears to dominate the tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A figure from behind facing a stone tower across a dusk square.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the claim into an image of the square facing the tower.
storyboard.addedInformation: The everyman stands for the square.

image.subject: a historian's hands turning the pages of an open 19th-century archive ledger with handwritten columns of figures in a quiet library

storyboard.claim: The popular myth differs from the documented record.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hands turning pages of an archive ledger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the myth to the evidence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The record is a ledger, not a rebellion.

image.subject: a row of gilded palace windows lit at dusk on a grand imperial street in Vienna, a carriage waiting at the entrance

storyboard.claim: The Rothschilds financed empires, not revolutions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grand imperial palace at dusk with a waiting carriage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the empire the record says they supported.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the financing in an imperial capital.

storyboard.claim: If they could break the king, why not do it?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A direct question in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the puzzle the next beat answers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the paradox.

image.subject: an old royal bond with a faded crown seal, tied with a ribbon, lying on a counting-house desk beside a sealed letter of demand

storyboard.claim: New governments would default on old royal debts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A faded royal bond tied with ribbon on a desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers why the network needed the kings.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the debts that would go unpaid.

image.subject: an 18th-century Frankfurt merchant-banker in his fifties, stout, dark wool coat, round spectacles, ledger in hand, standing in a counting house

storyboard.claim: The Rothschilds became stabilizers of the monarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The banker with ledger, standing in a counting house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers who would pay the bonds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the named banker on screen as the stabilizer.

image.subject: a royal palace at dusk with lit windows, seen across a river, the palace's stone walls reflected in still water

storyboard.claim: The network's survival depended on the survival of the state towers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lit royal palace reflected in still water.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the state tower the network depended on.
storyboard.addedInformation: The palace is the state whose survival matters.

image.subject: a courier in a dark travelling coat arriving at a Frankfurt bank doorway with a leather satchel of letters, a stagecoach waiting in the street

storyboard.claim: Kings had to stay on thrones so interest kept arriving in Frankfurt and London.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A courier with a satchel at a bank door beside a waiting stagecoach.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the reasoning in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the courier carrying interest payments.

image.subject: a counting-house window overlooking a crowded town square at dusk, ledgers stacked on the sill and revolutionary banners hanging across the street

storyboard.claim: The square ended up financing the tower and became the status quo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A counting-house window looking onto a dusk square.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pulls the square and the tower into one view.
storyboard.addedInformation: The counting house sits between the square and the state.

storyboard.claim: The kings kept their crowns and the network got rich.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two outcomes listed in plain type.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the bargain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the two sides of the deal.

image.subject: a long wooden table in a candle-lit lodge room, an old map of Europe spread across it with thin red and blue threads pinned between cities

storyboard.claim: Hidden networks govern visible structures.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A map of Europe with red and blue threads pinned between cities.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the banking story to the general claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: The threads show the hidden web.

storyboard.claim: Leave the royal courts for a mundane setting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A place label in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Europe's courts to the reformatory.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the next location.

image.subject: a dusty classroom chalkboard in a 1930s girls' reformatory school in Hudson, New York, wooden desks empty in the late afternoon light

storyboard.claim: The setting is a chalkboard at a New York girls' reformatory in 1932.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dusty chalkboard in an empty 1930s classroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves to the new setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets place and year.

image.subject: a 1930s American psychiatrist in his forties, dark three-piece suit with the tie loosened, chalk in hand, standing beside a dusty classroom chalkboard

storyboard.claim: Jacob Moreno invented the sociological study of networks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A psychiatrist in a 1930s suit with chalk beside a chalkboard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the person from the setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the psychiatrist who founded network sociology.

image.subject: a dusty chalkboard covered in tangled, chaotic webs of chalk lines linking rows of circles

storyboard.claim: Moreno drew tangled webs of circles and lines called sociograms.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chalkboard with a tangled web of circles and lines.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the drawing the psychiatrist just made.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the form of a sociogram.

image.subject: a group of young women in plain 1930s dresses seated on a wooden bench in a reformatory courtyard, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: Sociograms mapped the hidden social dynamics of the girls in the reformatory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Young women on a bench in a courtyard, seen from behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the people the chalk diagram maps.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the mapped group on screen.

left.label: HATE
left.subject: two chalk circles joined by a short hard red line on a dusty blackboard

right.label: FRIENDSHIP
right.subject: two chalk circles joined by a short soft blue line on a dusty blackboard

storyboard.claim: Red lines show hate and rejection, blue lines show friendship and attraction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two chalk pairs of circles, one joined by red, one by blue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the colour code of the sociogram.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines the two line types.

image.subject: an iron-railed gate of a 1930s reformatory standing open onto a dirt road at dusk, empty footprints in the dust

storyboard.claim: The school faced an epidemic of girls running away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open reformatory gate onto a dusty road at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the crisis that the chalk diagram addresses.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the exit the runaways took.

storyboard.claim: The administration looked only at the official structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three things the administration examined, listed in plain type.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE LAYOUT / THE RULES / THE RECORDS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the administration was clueless.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three official things they checked.

image.subject: a 1930s office bulletin board with a pinned organisation chart of boxes and lines carrying typed names

storyboard.claim: The administration was looking at the org chart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A pinned organisation chart on an office board.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the official structure just listed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the chart being looked at.

image.subject: a shelf of printed official rulebooks beside a single open notebook with pencil lines drawn across its pages

storyboard.claim: The official rules did not matter; the invisible network did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Rulebooks on a shelf and an open notebook with pencil lines.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the official structure to the invisible one.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notebook is the network being traced.

image.subject: a young woman in a plain 1930s dress answering questions across a wooden table while a psychiatrist in a dark suit writes notes

storyboard.claim: By asking the girls who they liked and hated, the hidden web emerged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An interview across a table, the writer taking notes.
storyboard.onScreenText: WHO THEY LIKED / WHO THEY HATED
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the method behind the diagram.
storyboard.addedInformation: The method was asking the girls directly.

image.subject: a hand-drawn network map spread across a wooden desk, a few dark hub circles larger than the rest and one lonely circle set apart

storyboard.claim: The map reveals hubs of influence, isolated girls and rumour channels.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A hand-drawn network map with hubs and one isolated circle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes what the map shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the isolated node and rumour channels.

image.subject: an ordinary person in plain clothes, mid-thirties, seen from behind, standing in a modern open-plan office with small groups of coworkers talking

storyboard.claim: Your success is governed by invisible networks at your workplace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A figure from behind in an office with small groups talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the reformatory lesson to the listener.
storyboard.addedInformation: Brings the idea to the viewer's own office.

storyboard.claim: Influence is not about the official org chart or title.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bold closing line in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the workplace application.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dismisses the title as the measure of influence.

storyboard.claim: Who do people go to for help or the real story? Almost never the person at the top.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question in text.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE REAL STORY / NOT THE TOP
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks who the real hub is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the answer about centrality.

image.subject: a chalk diagram of seven small circles where one circle in the middle connects a line to every other circle

storyboard.claim: Your position depends on betweenness centrality in the hidden network.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seven circles with one central node connected to all.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the measure the previous question pointed to.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the central node as the betweenness hub.
